title: Three-Way Hypothesis Contrast: Sabah Fold-Thrust Belt
subtitle: Which story breaks reality more?
eureka_reframe: The question is not 'is there a slab or not.' The question is: 'Did oceanic crust subduct, or did continental crust subduct? And which story contradicts reality more?'

A_oceanic_past.name: Oceanic crust subducted in the past (proto-South China Sea). Relict slab may exist at depth. Now dead.
A_oceanic_past.story: South China Sea opened, spread, created oceanic crust. Spreading stopped. That oceanic crust subducted beneath Borneo/Sabah in the Miocene (~15 Ma). The slab consumed itself. A relict fragment may sit at >200 km depth, cold and dead.

B_continental_subducted.name: Continental crust subducted beneath Sabah (current belief drift).
B_continental_subducted.story: South China Sea spreading stopped. The continental margin 'subducted' beneath Sabah. The fold-thrust belt is the surface expression of continental subduction.

C_active_slab_today.name: An oceanic slab is actively driving Sabah deformation right now.
C_active_slab_today.story: A live oceanic slab sits beneath the fold-thrust belt, driving present-day deformation, seismicity, and basin evolution.

1st.reason: Oceanic crust is denser than mantle (ρ=2.94 vs 3.3 — wait, actually oceanic is LIGHTER than mantle at surface. But as it subducts and metamorphoses to eclogite (ρ=3.33), it becomes denser. This is WHY oceanic subduction works: the slab starts light enough to be pushed, then becomes heavy enough to sink on its own.
1st.buoyancy: WORKS — negative buoyancy after eclogite transition
1st.plate_history: CONSISTENT — SCS spreading (32-15 Ma) then cessation fits
1st.timing: CONSISTENT — Miocene consumption, no present-day arc needed
1st.seismicity: CONSISTENT — shallow only, no deep zone needed for dead slab

2nd.reason: If the slab were still active, we'd see: deep seismicity, volcanic arc, trench, heat flow anomaly. None present.
2nd.buoyancy: WORKS in principle — but no evidence of activity
2nd.plate_history: CONTRADICTS — SCS stopped spreading at ~15 Ma, no driving mechanism
2nd.timing: CONTRADICTS — 15 Ma of no subduction signal

3rd.reason: Continental crust (ρ=2.66) is 24% lighter than mantle (ρ=3.3). It FLOATS. It resists subduction. The only known case (India-Asia) required 50+ Ma of extreme convergence at 50 mm/yr. Sabah convergence is <10 mm/yr. There is no force vector to push buoyant continental crust into dense mantle.
3rd.plate_history: CONTRADICTS — no driving mechanism for continental subduction
3rd.seismicity: CONTRADICTS — no deep seismicity, no HP metamorphism

buoyancy_physics.note: Buoyancy is physics, not geology opinion. Density is measured, not interpreted. [OBS]

oceanic_gabbro.buoyancy_vs_mantle: LIGHTER than mantle (Δρ = -0.36) — can be pushed down by slab push

after_eclogite_transition.buoyancy_vs_mantle: DENSER than mantle (Δρ = +0.03) — sinks on its own
after_eclogite_transition.mechanism: Eclogite transition at 40-80 km depth. Once started, slab pulls itself down. Self-sustaining subduction.

continental_granite.buoyancy_vs_mantle: MUCH LIGHTER than mantle (Δρ = -0.64) — resists subduction violently
continental_granite.even_at_high_P: Even at eclogite-facies (ρ~3.0-3.1), still lighter than mantle. No self-sustaining pull.
continental_granite.known_cases: India-Asia collision (50+ Ma, 50 mm/yr convergence). ONE case in Earth history. Required extreme forces.

sabah_observed.note: Matches CONTINENTAL crust signature — but this is the FILL, not the slab. The fill is collision-derived sediments, not subducted continental crust.
sabah_observed.interpretation: The observed density matches accretionary wedge material, NOT subducted continental crust

continental_subduction.analogy: Like claiming a beach ball sinks in water. Continental crust FLOATS on mantle. You need extreme forces (India-Asia) to even partially subduct it. Sabah has no such forces.
continental_subduction.known_analogues: India-Asia (ONLY case — 50+ Ma, 50 mm/yr, ongoing). Sabah: <10 mm/yr, no extreme convergence.

active_oceanic_slab.analogy: Like claiming a dead man is still running. The slab existed, but it's gone. The corpse is the relict at depth.
active_oceanic_slab.known_analogues: Many — Cascadia, Andes, Japan (active slabs have clear signatures)

past_oceanic_slab.analogy: Like saying a river used to flow here. Oceanic crust subducted, consumed itself, left an accretionary prism as evidence.
past_oceanic_slab.known_analogues: Many — Mediterranean (Tethys consumed), Caribbean, Banda Arc

sabah_reality.what_the_fold_thrust_belt_actually_is: An accretionary prism built by collision between the Dangerous Grounds (continental rifted margin) and the Borneo continental margin. NOT a subduction complex. NOT evidence of continental subduction.
sabah_reality.what_drove_deformation: Collision-accretion. The Crocker Formation is an accretionary wedge of deep-marine sediments scraped off the subducting oceanic plate and stacked against the continental margin.
sabah_reality.what_happened_to_the_slab: The Proto-South China Sea oceanic crust subducted beneath Borneo in the Oligocene-Miocene. By ~15 Ma, it was consumed. The system transitioned from subduction to collision. The fold-thrust belt is the COLLISION product, not the subduction product.
sabah_reality.what_people_confuse: The accretionary prism (collision product) gets misinterpreted as evidence of ongoing subduction. The basin fill (flexural loading from collision) gets misinterpreted as slab-induced subsidence. The shallow seismicity (crustal deformation) gets misinterpreted as slab-interface coupling.
sabah_reality.continental_subduction_narrative: Is a category error. Continental crust did NOT subduct. It COLLIDED. The distinction matters: subduction = one plate dives under another. Collision = two buoyant plates smash together and build mountains. Sabah is the mountain-building part.

buoyancy.oceanic: WORKS — negative buoyancy after eclogite transition [OBS]
buoyancy.continental: FAILS — 24% lighter than mantle, resists subduction [OBS]

metamorphism.oceanic: Expected blueschist/eclogite in subduction channel — absent in Sabah (fits consumed slab) [DER]
metamorphism.continental: Expected massive HP/UHP belts (like Dabie-Sulu in China) — absent [OBS]
metamorphism.verdict: Neither shows present-day HP, but continental requires it and doesn't have it

seismicity.oceanic: No deep zone needed for dead slab [DER]
seismicity.continental: Deep seismicity REQUIRED for continental subduction — absent [OBS]
seismicity.verdict: Continental model predicts something that doesn't exist

geometry.continental: Vergence WRONG — fold-thrust verges NE, not SW [OBS]
geometry.verdict: Continental model requires polarity reversal with no kinematic support

timing.continental: No convergence event to drive continental subduction [OBS]
timing.verdict: Continental model has no driving mechanism

final_verdict.why: It violates buoyancy (Archimedes), metamorphic petrology (no HP belts), seismicity (no deep zone), structural geometry (wrong vergence), and plate tectonics (no driving mechanism). It has 9 total violations vs 5 for active oceanic slab and 0 for past oceanic slab.
final_verdict.the_eureka: Sabah geology tells a story of oceanic subduction that ENDED in collision — not continental subduction that never happened. The accretionary prism (Crocker Formation) is the EVIDENCE of past oceanic subduction, not proof of ongoing or continental subduction. People who claim 'continental crust subducted' are fighting Archimedes, metamorphic petrology, structural geology, and plate tectonics simultaneously.
final_verdict.what_geoX_proves: Contrast analysis can rank hypotheses by physics consistency, not narrative sophistication. The 'continental subduction' story is the most narratively convenient but the most physically absurd.
